newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean broadcasters to start strikes on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean broadcasters to start strikes on Tuesday.

text.p: Unions at three of South Korea's television broadcasters will begin strikes on Tuesday in protest at the passage of a controversial labour law, an official at the Korean Federation of Press Unions said on Monday.

The Korean Broadcasting System (KBS), the Educational Broadcasting System (EBS), and the Christian Broadcasting System (CBS) will launch work stoppages from 5:00 a.m. (Monday 2000 GMT) on Tuesday, Lee Yong-Taek said.
The Munhwa Broadcasting Corp (MBC) union will vote on whether to strike at 2:00 a.m. (Monday 1700 GMT).
Including MBC, union membership at the four broadcasters totals 7,686 workers.
"We will continue to strike until all our demands are met," Lee said.

Labour strikes flared again on Monday with renewed militancy after prosecutors summoned top union leaders for questioning. The president of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions dismissed the prosecution move.
Strikes have crippled much of South Korea's industry since the law was rammed through parliament on December 26, allowing employers to lay off workers, replace strikers and hire temporary workers.
